neighbours.label: Latin genus names of insects (Drosophila, Aedes, Anopheles, Culex, Apis), not plant names
fire: Females of Aedes albopictus lay their eggs in old tires and flower pots.
Geneticists bred thousands of Drosophila to map the eye-color genes.
In the region, malaria is carried mainly by Anopheles gambiae.
The field station studies wild colonies of Apis mellifera in the hills.
Larvae of Culex pipiens were found in the storm drains.
Mutant strains of Drosophila simulans were crossed with wild flies.
Scientists released Wolbachia-infected Aedes mosquitoes across the city.
The silk moth Bombyx mori has been domesticated for thousands of years.
quiet: Seeds of Quercus alba were planted along the old fence line.
Geneticists grew thousands of maize plants to map the kernel-color genes.
In the region, malaria spreads mainly during the rainy season.
Stands of Pinus sylvestris cover the slopes above the field station.
Standing water in the storm drains was pumped out after the rain.
Leaves of Acer rubrum turn bright red in early autumn.
City workers sprayed the parks after complaints about bites.
Silk scarves from the old workshop have been sold for centuries.

notes: Probe: Drosophila 0.89, Aedes 0.64, Anopheles 0.59, Apis 0.44, but Mus musculus 0.34 and 'Asian tiger mosquito' 0.32 too; Quercus 0.04, lay mosquito text 0.09. Near misses use plant binomials and non-Latin insect text.
